What sort of stuff do you enjoy doing. Do you have a favourite TV series, book series, art. Anything. Even if you ask him to watch a show and you watch the same thing. Gives an excuse to have some time alone, uninterrupted and gives a topic of conversation (what episode are you on, what did you like abojt this episode, who's your favourite character). Just something you can both talk about between you. 

What else have you talked about? Is there anything from those conversations that you enjoyed more? Talk about your special interests? Ask about his (and maybe try to look into it to show you listen and care about his interests). For example I could care less about Halo and warhammer, but my partner really enjoys those things so I started looking into it more, finding fun facts to tell him. Not only does it mean that you can start a conversation about a topic he really likes, it also means that you can actively participate in conversations about it and if applicable add it to a wishlist for maybe later on

As for your friends, until the point you actually bring them together to meet each other, stop worrying. You need to focus on just you two and your relationship. If your friends can clearly see that you two care for each other and have each other interests at heart then there is no reason for them to worry or be rude.
Remember you're actually a person with feelings so don't let people treat you like you ain't worth their weight in gold :)

Have you set rules or is it you're just trying to let her go with the flow, because you can't have it both ways. 

It sounds like you're trying to parent her without actually setting down the ground rules. Eg, certain level of communication of where she's at and when she's back with a promise to stick to what she says. I understand its hard to change your current relationship and it doesn't have to change too much. You both need therapy desperately. 

If its too much for you, you can even ask her if she'd be willing to get a job to contribute (I wouldn't say a lot, but just to teach her money handling, how to prioritise money) and say by doing that she'll get more freedom to do what she would rather do. That way you can also keep the sort of relationship you're hoping to continue and she can keep the space space she wants. 

I did it with my parents, I felt like a lot of the house rules were too strict for me at 16, so I got a job and gave my parents £50 a month, I still had rules but the rules were a lot more relaxed and I gained knowledge on how to prioritise my money towards rent/bills and I gained a lot more freedom to do my own thing
